title: Bad News Reaches the Palace
overview: A Jewish official serving the king of Persia hears that Jerusalem lies unprotected and in ruins, and he responds with days of grief and a long prayer.

parts.label: News from Jerusalem (vv. 1-3)
parts.note: Nehemiah lives in Susa, a royal city of the Persian Empire, when visitors bring news of the Jews who had returned home after exile. Jerusalem's wall is still broken and its gates burned, leaving the people open to attack and mockery; scholars are unsure whether this damage was old or from a more recent attack.

parts.label: Days of grief (v. 4)
parts.note: Nehemiah weeps and goes without food for days while he prays. Fasting was a common way to show deep sorrow and to plead seriously with God.

parts.label: Praise and confession (vv. 5-7)
parts.note: He begins by naming God as great and faithful to his covenant, meaning the binding promise God made with Israel. Then he admits that the people, including himself and his own family, have broken God's laws given through Moses.

parts.label: Reminding God of a promise (vv. 8-10)
parts.note: Nehemiah sums up warnings and promises found in Israel's law: unfaithfulness would lead to scattering, but turning back would lead to being gathered home. He calls the people the ones God rescued by his great power, which most readers take as a reference to the escape from Egypt.

parts.label: A request and a reveal (v. 11)
parts.note: He asks for success before "this man," and only now explains that this man is the king, because Nehemiah is the king's cupbearer. A cupbearer served the king his drink, a trusted and important post that gave him regular personal access to the king.

think: When you hear bad news about a place or people you care about but are far away from, what do you actually do with that feeling?
